title: Preserving physical information in transferable wind-power event measurements

data_availability: Processed, pseudonymized SCADA for seven archives and 333 turbines is openly available at https://github.com/longjingpy/wind-power-event-protocol-audit/releases/tag/v0.3.0. The bundle contains 7,548,467 regular-grid rows with normalized power, turbine wind, quality flags, chronological splits and relative clocks. Original turbine names, direct location fields and absolute dates are excluded; the identifier and clock policy is documented with the data. Metadata, a data dictionary, a complete file index and verification records accompany the release. Original public sources include the Greek monitoring archive (doi:10.5281/zenodo.14546480), SDWPF (doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.24798654), La Haute Borne and Hill of Towie. Original provider terms and attribution remain applicable. Analysis scripts, selected checkpoints and aggregate results are available in the repository.
code_availability: Analysis scripts, targeted tests, selected-checkpoint reproduction and aggregate results are available at https://github.com/longjingpy/wind-power-event-protocol-audit. The repository distinguishes verified reproduction paths from outstanding full-workflow integration.
abstract: Wind-power events are useful when the distinctions they retain remain physically meaningful at the time of a decision. We introduce a protocol-aware framework that tests event measurements through detection, matching, representation and evaluation. Across seven wind-farm archives comprising 333 turbines, 17 detector configurations and six representations, plus an instrumented French site, matched trajectories reveal a stable structural reference while exposing information that angular encoding can discard. In the signed-domain Gramian angular field used here, opposite trajectories share one image; reserving a polarity coordinate within a six-dimensional representation protects their directional distinction. Chronological calibration against independent LiDAR measurements raises directional AUROC from 0.494/0.477 to 0.890/0.905 at two turbines. Three observers assess the same 320 real windows. In a separate observed-price experiment, historical event information reduces two-hour gross imbalance debits by 4.5%, while large-ramp periods account for 54–71% of persistence debits. These results establish a task-aware principle: preserve distinctions that survive protocol changes, verify them against independent physical measurements and evaluate them at the decision timescale.
highlights: Protocol-aware measurement separates event stability from physical information.
Protecting polarity restores wind-tendency discrimination after angular encoding.
Independent LiDAR tests connect event representations to measured wind changes.
Historical event information reduces two-hour gross imbalance debits by 4.5%.
Three observers anchor event-presence evaluation across 320 real windows.
